chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Catlett's $500 fee, Nellie Lutcher on the Lena Horne date, and Dave Barbour
summary: At the Capitol Theatre run with Lena, Catlett got $500 a week and recommended his wife Nellie Lutcher as pianist for the recording session; Dave Barbour helped pick non-studio musicians.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Another time I had the pleasure of using Big Syd Catlett was Lena Horn on this Capital. He was playing -- you know, I should name that eight pieces the -- I can't think of a good name to describe that, the eight millionaires for those weeks, 'cause this is the money they got. In fact, --
-- Big Syd, when I asked him how much money did he want, he who was it for? said, it was (inaudible). I said, plus for Lena Horn. He said $500.00 a week.
Lena knew him, she said, "Pay him." (Inaudible) do about it, so he was just paying.
And he got just that. Got this bad
How many weeks did that thing -- gig last?

This was at the Capital Theater, which was an MGM house. I think that gig lasted four or either six weeks. And of course, we had Xavier Cugat and his band there, Robert Ralph Walker and Lena Horn, what an the attractions. So while we were there, we had a session for the recording session, you know, for Lena Horn, and I made most of the arrangements that were recorded, and I remember distinctly I had a couple of arrangements there that he didn't conduct them, and I needed another piano player. So Big Syd said, "Hey, man, I can get you a piano player that can read your stuff here, and she doesn't live very far from here." He said, "It's my wife." I said, "Who's that?" He said, Nella Letcher. MR. : Nella Letcher, yeah. MR. HENDERSON: So this is when he called her up, and this is when I had the pleasure of having Nella Letcher.

She came in and did a good job, and I could confine my activities to the conductor of the band (inaudible) recorded, so that was great, and old Syd was out of sight. So -- let's see -- if I remember correctly, Syd made a few dates on the road, but not many. He was another like Benny Martin. He didn't dig the road too much.
He wanted to stay home. Yeah. What about Peggy Lee? Dave Barbour? They were on that recording --
-- was on the session, in that band with Lena Horne. And we had another guy that was on there, (inaudible). You know the guy that wrote Little Darlin'?
Neil Hefty was on there. Yeah, Neil was on there.

I had some great musicians. In fact, Dave Barbour, now that it's been called to my attention, he was instrumental in the (inaudible) the personnel for this particular date. And it worked out beautiful.
Uh-huh. He was with Capital, I think.
Yes. Yes. And he (inaudible) the musicians that weren't tied up with the studios, that could make positions so that it wouldn't tie up with his (inaudible). So it's been a great experience for me.
